$comment: The project's version and its player-facing release notes. Newest first; order in this list IS the version order. Read by client/changelog.py for /puzzle changelog, requested privately. Adding a release means putting it at the top. Keep `changes` to things a player can see.

changes: **Finishing a puzzle while the server restarts no longer loses it.** A daily sheet or a rush handed in at that moment says **Reconnecting…** and tries again for up to about fifteen seconds, instead of failing at once. A practice clear tries again the same way, without the message.
**1v1 says when the server is updating** and asks you to open the lobby again, instead of only saying the connection closed. After any dropped duel connection, **Duel** works again straight away.

**An "Update ready" chip appears in the header when a new version of the activity is out.** Reload when you're done: it never shows in the middle of a run, a rush or a duel, and it never reloads by itself.
**A sheet you finish after the daily reset is no longer judged against the new day's puzzle.** The activity says that day is over and loads today's puzzles.

**A bot command sent while the bot is finishing others before a restart** now gets "Restarting — try again in a few seconds." instead of no answer. While the bot is fully down, between the old one closing and the new one connecting, Discord still says the application did not respond.

**Every line you find now lands in the puzzle's Solutions**: a puzzle from Explore, and a replay of a daily you have already solved (**Play again**), as well as the daily itself. Until now only the daily run reached the Solutions menu, so solving a puzzle another way afterwards left no trace. A new line found this way also counts on the Discoveries board.

**Reopening the activity now asks Discord to reuse your existing permission approval.** The sign-in still verifies your identity and server. First-time access, changed permissions or a revoked approval can still show the consent screen.

**Release notes now appear only when you ask.** Use `/puzzle play` to open the activity without posting a changelog to the channel. Use `/puzzle changelog` to see the five most recent changes privately, or set `count` from 1 to 20.

**`/puzzle` now posts a short message and the activity link.** The daily puzzle summary, difficulty tiers, solve count and streak reminder are gone from its Discord reply. Open the activity to see today's puzzles.

**The archive now has a Players table and a recent-solves feed.** Sort players by days solved, best streak, puzzles cleared, lines found or best rush; search by name and narrow to a server. Each profile shows per-tier solve rates and times, a calendar and puzzles cleared. The Solves page lists daily solves by tier, server and puzzle. Players who choose to hide still appear only as "a player" and have no profile.

**To leave yourself off the site**, open the activity's Settings → On the web and turn on **Hide me on db.tetrisatuci.org**. Your results there then read "a player", within a few minutes, and you can turn it off again whenever you like. The game's own boards are unchanged.

**Anyone can run `/archive sync` now**, not only officers — it pulls new puzzles in from the club's sheet and makes them playable. It runs at most once every 10 minutes, shared by every server. Ask too soon and the bot tells you, privately, when the last sync started and when the next one can.
The ten-minute wait still holds if the bot's clock moves backwards and its database cannot save the new sync start.

**db.tetrisatuci.org now shows how every finished day went**: each Discord server's daily boards, tier by tier, and rush board; the all-time boards, Discoveries among them; each puzzle's hand-ins, solves and times; and a page for each player with their solved days, streaks, best rush and lines found. Players appear by the name the game shows, and servers by their Discord name once somebody signs in from there. Today is never shown. The game keeps its own leaderboards, profile and solutions.

**New setting: Hide me on db.tetrisatuci.org**, under Settings → On the web. With it on, your results on the site say "a player" and you have no page there. The site catches up within a few minutes, and you can turn it off at any time. It hides you on the site only: the game's boards still show you, and a copy of the site saved before you turned it on keeps what it had.

**Players' alternate lines are now public on db.tetrisatuci.org**, on each puzzle's page, for finished days, with no name on them. Beta 0.3 said a puzzle you had not solved kept its answers to themselves; on the site that is no longer true, so open a puzzle's answers there only when you want them. In the game nothing changes: a puzzle's solutions still open once you have solved it.

**The club's puzzle archive is on the web at https://db.tetrisatuci.org** — every club puzzle the daily deals from, with its board, to search by title, author, set, difficulty or length, no sign-in needed. Open one to step through its maker's answer, which stays hidden until you press **Show the answer**. Each finished day is listed too, with the puzzles it dealt (never today's), and the whole archive downloads as one SQLite file. Puzzles written by players are not listed there.

**`/internships` and `/bennxt` are gone from this bot.** Internship alerts now come from a separate bot, **DIAYN**, in the club's Discord server, and everyone who had alerts on has been carried over to it. DIAYN sends alerts as direct messages, so keep Direct Messages from the club server's members turned on. Use `/internships` on DIAYN to see or change yours. The puzzles and every other command here work as before.

**A flick slams, and a placement waits to be locked.** A fast, straight-down flick now hard-drops the piece from the seat it showed when the stroke began — the slam is one command, and a beat of stillness ends it: drag to a seat, rest a moment, and the drag becomes a placement there rather than a flick anywhere. A placement then locks only after the piece rests for about three quarters of a second with nobody touching the screen — the wait counts against your clock, like any other pause. A ring shows the wait; putting a hand back on the piece holds it; and any key press — a hard drop, a turn, an undo — cancels the wait and plays the falling piece itself, exactly as the keyboard always plays. Tapping a piece you have parked turns it where it sits, and taking a placement back leaves the piece and its preview turning together. A stroke that begins with the piece past the board's edge is not a slam — nothing is shown there to drop — so the piece resets on the release, exactly as a drag released off the board does. The same gestures work under a mouse as under a finger.

**The page no longer highlights text on touch unless it is meant to be read.** A drifting finger or a long-press can no longer select anything on the play screen — board, HUD, header, the puzzle-title strip, toast messages — and the same goes for the rest of the page: one rule now keeps every surface gesture-clean instead of each surface asking its own way out. What still selects is what exists to be read and copied — the goal sentence, solution walkthroughs, the settings sheet — and anything you type into keeps its caret and its text.

**No more daily ping.** The day after each puzzle, the bot used to reply to that day's `/puzzle` announcement with how it went, mentioning the people who played, so they got a notification every day. That post is switched off. Your own solves and streak, and the leaderboards, are still in the activity; the server's streak and the finished day's board were only in that post, so they went with it.

**New puzzles from the club's sheet show up as soon as an officer syncs them** — in Explore and duels straight away, and in the daily rotation from the next day. Nothing about a day you are already playing changes, and nobody gets disconnected.

**A puzzle can ask for a spin that clears no lines.** #123 “style” says “Perform 3 Spins” and its own answer spins three times — but one of those spins clears nothing, and the game had no name for that, so only two of the three were ever counted. It is named now, and style asks for all three. No other puzzle changes: a spin that clears nothing counts toward a goal only where the goal actually asks for one.

**A puzzle keeps its answer until you solve it.** Opening one from Explore and failing it used to show the maker's solution anyway — the walkthrough appeared beside a board nobody had cracked. It now arrives the moment you solve the puzzle, and not before. Puzzles you solved earlier are unaffected: their answers are still there whenever you go back.

**Playing on a phone no longer hides the piece under your finger.** On a touch screen a drag carries the piece from where it is — it never jumps to your finger — and the piece travels farther than the finger, about one and a half squares per finger square in every direction, so the bottom rows come to your finger instead of the other way around. The travel is virtual: a drag may wander off the board and back out to exactly where it was. Letting go on the board buys exactly the seat shown — one that will not fit parks the piece there as a dashed preview drawn over the stack, and the next drag continues from that seat; past the edge the piece falls again. Finish a placement a stroke at a time.

**The play screen fits a phone.** The board was a ten-pixel sliver with its side panels taking two thirds of the width; on a narrow screen — a square one too — hold, goal and the queue fold into one slim column beside a full-height board: panels compacted, the attack meter folded into the goal it chases, and the queue one piece per row, filling the column and showing the puzzle's whole order instead of a teaser. The board takes the space back, roughly three times as large. The undo and redo buttons stay behind on desktop: the finger taps and the keyboard do that job now. Desktop layout is unchanged.

**Two-finger tap to undo, three to redo.** On a touch screen the undo and redo buttons now have gestures beside them: a quick tap of two fingers takes back the last placement, three puts it back. Drags and long-presses are untouched — the chord only fires on a genuine tap.

**Officers can pull the puzzle spreadsheet into the archive from Discord**, with `/archive sync`. It reads the sheet and files every puzzle it can replay, and everything it writes stays unpublished until somebody reviews it — so it changes nothing a player is served. `/archive sync dry_run:True` reports what would change without writing. Anyone not on the officer list is turned away privately.

**A leaderboards page.** Seven boards — today, rush records, daily solves, current and longest-ever streaks, archive progress, and lines nobody had found. Every name on them opens that player's profile.
**A profile**, behind your own picture in the top right: what you have solved, how long it took, your rush totals, your streak, and every alternate line you have found.
**Explore ticks the puzzles you have solved**, and every solve counts — a daily, a rush puzzle, or one from Explore. Practice used to vanish the moment you closed it.
**A puzzle's solutions open from inside it, once you have solved it**: every recorded way through, who found each one, and what it sent. Puzzles you have not solved keep their answers to themselves.
**Reading a solution back is a timeline**, with a mark on every placement that clears lines, arrow keys to step, and the next piece shown as a ghost.
**Discoveries is one board**, every server, all time — and **every line you find counts** rather than one per puzzle. A line counts if it solves the puzzle or sends more attack than it asked for.
Editing a puzzle no longer takes back credit for a line somebody found on it.

**Four puzzles that could not be solved from the keyboard now can be.** On a polymer T-spin the same squares score two ways depending on the kick you rotated in on, and dragging quietly took the good one. #3, #6, #17 and #92.
**#115 “twirl” asks for the TST it always said it did**, rather than enforcing a TSD and refusing the one line its goal describes.
The day now holds **four** puzzles, not three: a new **extreme** tier above hard, for the ones rated five squares and up.
Solved a puzzle? The walkthrough of the answer is back. It had been coming up empty on the live server, which was a missing file rather than a missing feature.
**Hand it in** asks before it ends a rush. It files the run and discards the puzzles left in it, and there is no undo.
Finding a line nobody had found is credited properly. Playing the puzzle's own intended solution no longer reports a discovery.
Finishing a daily no longer says the sheet could not be filed when it was filed, scored, and already on the board.
Holding at the end of the queue no longer hands you a tetromino the puzzle never offered.
A puzzle's required clears now come from its own recorded answer, so the line its maker played is always one that counts.
Puzzles can now require the clears their goal names — a goal that says "2 TSDs" is no longer satisfied by any line that reaches the attack target.
Your progress toward those clears shows on the board while you play.
Solved a daily? **Play again** replays it unscored, so your filed run stands.
The **Solved!** stamp now clears itself once there is a solution to read.
`/report` now answers in the channel rather than only to whoever sent it, and allows 15 reports an hour instead of 3.
